**Daily Devotional**

**May 6**

* 18 The eyes of your understanding being enlightened; that ye may know what is the hope of his calling, and what the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints, (Ephesians 1:18 KJV)*

The “eyes of your understanding” is talking about the eyes of our heart, or spiritual eyes. We have to have our understanding, or spiritual eyes, opened by the Lord to be able to perceive spiritual truths (Luke 24:25). The Holy Spirit gives the born again believer the understanding to be able to discern spiritual matters, but the world can not understand the things of God (Colossians 1:26).

Notice that this verse says, “the hope of his calling”, not our calling. Through our faith in Christ, we have become joint heirs with Christ of everything that He is entitled to (Galatians 3:29). What a deal, to be sons and heirs through Christ of all that is Gods. Wow!

Notice that this inheritance is in the saints, not out there in heaven somewhere. If we only knew what all this inheritance consisted of, that is already in us, we would be astounded (Romans 8:18), as it is the very Glory of God. Help us Lord, to understand what we already have been given through your grace.

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com

This is me nitpicking about some majorly irritating flaws with the movie. Spoilers, obviously.

Let's start with the proposed cause of the zombies: radiation from a destroyed space probe that returned from orbiting Venus. That's exactly as dumb as superheroes being created from gamma rays or radioactive spider bites. It's comic book level schlock, and the movie spends way too much time on it. It would have been better left unexplained.

Next we come to the characters. None of them have any depth. There's what the movie at first appears to establish as the main female protagonist. She's a hysterical woman who hardly says or does anything while everyone around her talks and does everything. She's one dimensional and totally unsympathetic. Just like all the other characters. We have a cowardly middle aged man. You can tell because he acts cowardly. It's all he does. Then there's his bitter contrarian wife and mother who acts contrarian and is sort-of motherly, her sick daughter who lays in the basement being sick, the young well meaning simpleton who acts like a well meaning simpleton, his wholesome dumb "good girl" girlfriend who acts like a wholesome dumb good girl (but yet still manages to make it look like a ridiculously thin act, probably just due to poor acting skills). And finally we come to the brash hero type who takes charge. And yes, that's all he does too. He's at least somewhat interesting in spite of being poorly written like all the rest simply because he actually does shit. He's like the John Wayne of the movie. He kicks ass and takes names. I'd say he's the only halfway intelligent character, but...

The whole movie didn't have to happen. They could easily outrun the zombies, or even just walk away from them at a brisk pace. Stopping at a house to box themselves in, turning on the lights, and making noise, were literally the worst possible set of things they could do. All they did was attract more and more zombies in large enough numbers to pose a real danger to themselves. If they had just kept moving, they would have been fine. Or, if they had done as the coward suggested and stayed in the basement, quiet and out of sight, they wouldn't have attracted zombies. Even when the house was overrun, going in the basement worked. The door held, and eventually the zombies forgot what they were doing and walked away. The coward was right all along.

Fuck me, this movie was dumb as dirt.
